elements.section: Visibly Observed Photocrosslinking Reaction in Indolyl Based Pendant Liquid Crystalline Polymers: Synthesis and Optical Property

elements.text: ABSTRACT: Visibly observed photocrosslinkable pendant liquid crystalline polymers containing indolyl based chalcone were synthesized by free-radical polymerization and characterized spectroscopically. The differential scanning calorimetry and polarized optical microscopy were used to examine liquid crystalline property. The photocrosslinking and luminescence properties were monitored by UV-Vis spectrophotometer and spectrofluorimeter, respectively. It demonstrates the chalcone unit did not manifest cis trans-isomerization reaction along with 2p 2p photodimerization upon irradiation with UV light like other chalcones hitherto reported. The photocrosslinking was visibly monitored in solution through change of fluorescent color to colorless. The spacer lengths play a key role in the reaction. The fluorescence maximum was blue shifted around 70 nm in chloroform solution upon irradiation with UV light confirms the 2p 2p photodimerization of chalcone unit. VC 2009 Wiley Periodicals, Inc. elements.text: INTRODUCTION

Liquid crystalline materials have been studied for several decades in electrical and optical fields not only for scientific interests but also for their practical applications.<sup>1</sup> Photo-initiated polymerization has attracted long-standing interest of polymer chemists not only to understand basic mechanism and kinetics of polymerization, but also to fabricate photolithographic images for electronic and photonic applications.<sup>2</sup> Polymer film with functional groups such as photoisomerizable or photocrosslinkable groups were used for optical information storage, retardation film, photo-alignment layer for liquid crystal orientation and so forth.<sup>3</sup> Polymers containing olefinic double bond undergoes cycloaddition upon irradiation of UV light is one of the commonly used photoinduced reactions.<sup>4–6</sup> Recently, it has also been noticed that photocrosslinkable liquid crystalline polymers exploited as photo-alignment layer for liquid crystals, where the photodimerization occurs by exposure to UV light and their orientation adjusted by polarization direction of irradiated light.<sup>7–9</sup> Among many promising photocrosslinkable groups, chalcone has been well studied and expended in photocrosslinkable side-chain as well as main-chain polymers.<sup>10,11</sup> The preparation of functional materials with chalcone moiety has attracted attention attributable to afford high sensitivity to UV irradiation.<sup>12–14</sup> According to Woodward-Hoffmann rule, the photoinduced cycloaddition of two olefins to give their cyclobutane ring formation is allowed photochemically as 2p 2p reaction in the solid state when topological requirements such as molecular arrangements are fulfilled to minimize molecular motion referable to bimolecular reaction. Chalcone main- and side-chain polymers cross-link by 2p 2p cycloaddition reaction on illumination with UV light appear to possess promising photo-alignment characteristics.<sup>15,16</sup> The indolyl based chalcone unit containing side-chain liquid crystalline polymers are hitherto unreported. In the present work, we report the synthesis and optical property of indolyl based chalcone containing sidechain liquid crystalline polymers. The photocrosslinking reaction of chalcone was visibly observed by changing the color in solution from fluorescent to colorless is discussed.

EXPERIMENTAL
Materials

Methanol, ethanol, phenol, THF, diethyl ether, chloroform, triethylamine, dimethylformamide (DMF) (SRL, India), and other solvents were purified by reported procedures.<sup>17</sup> Acetone, sodium hydroxide, mathacrylic acid, hydroquinone, and 2,20-azobis(2-methylpropionitrile) (AIBN) (Merck, Germany) were used as received. 1,6-Hexanediol, 1,8-octanediol, 1,10-decanediol, 3-methylindole and 4-hydroxy acetophenone, 1,3-dicyclohexylcarbodimide (DCC), and 4-di(methylamino)pyridine (DMAP) (Fluka, Switzerland) were used as supplied. Methacryloylchloride and n-bromo-1-alkanols were prepared according to the reported procedures.<sup>18</sup> 4-(n-Hydroxyalkyloxy)benzoic acids (5–7) and 4-(n-methacryloyloxy alkyloxy) benzoic acids (8–10) were synthesized by reported procedures.<sup>19</sup>
Instrumentation

The infrared spectra were obtained on a Bruker IFS 66V Fourier transform spectrometer using KBr pellets. High-resolution $^ { 1 } \mathrm { H }$and $^ { 1 3 } \mathrm { C }$NMR spectra were recorded on a Bruker 300 MHz spectrometer in $\mathrm { C D C l _ { 3 } }$with TMS as an internal standard. The weight-average molecular weight $( \overline { { M _ { \mathrm { w } } } } )$, number-average molecular weight $( \overline { { M _ { \mathrm { n } } } } )$

and polydispersity $( \overline { { M _ { \mathrm { w } } } } / \overline { { M _ { \mathrm { n } } } } )$of the polymers were obtained on a PL-GPC model 210 chromatograph using THF as eluent at $2 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$and calibrated with polystyrene standard. DSC measurements were performed at a heating rate of 5 C/min up to 400 $^ \circ \mathrm { C }$on sample taken in an aluminium pan with a pierced lid, in dry nitrogen atmosphere with an empty pan as reference. The texture of sample was observed using a Euromax polarizing optical microscope equipped with a Linkem HFS-91 heating stage and a TP-93 temperature programmer. Small quantity of sample was placed between two thin glass cover slips, heated and cooled at the rate of 5 C/min and mesophases observed. The photographs were taken on a Nikon FM-10 camera and exposed on Kodak 200 film. The absorption spectra in spectroscopic grade chloroform solution and in thin film were measured on a Shimadzu UV-260 spectrophotometer. The photocrosslinking reaction was carried out using a 500- W high-pressure Hg lamp (Ushio SX-UI 5000) equipped with a cut filter (Sigma, UTVAF-35U) for UV irradiation (360 nm). Fluorescence spectra were measured on a Perkin–Elmer LS 45 fluorescence spectrofluorimeter with excitation near and absorption maximum of chalcone moiety, using 5 nm resolutions for both excitation and emission. The change in fluorescence of chalcone was carried out using similar filter of UV lights.

elements.text: Synthesis of Polymer Ia–IIc

The polymers were synthesized by free-radical solution addition polymerization from the respective monomers using AIBN as an initiator in THF at $6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$for 48 h. The typical procedure for the synthesis of polymer ia is as follows: The monomer ia (400 mg, 0.67 mol) and AIBN (2 wt %) were dissolved in dry THF (5 mL) and gentle steam ofnitrogen purged into the solution. The solution was kept in an oil bath at $6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$for 48 h. Then, the solution was cooled and poured into excess of methanol to precipitate the product. The crude polymer thus obtained was represipitated twice using chloroform and methanol. The purified polymer was dried at $4 5 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$under vacuum for 48 h to afford yellow colored solid. The remaining Ib–IIc was also prepared by adopting similar procedure as of Ia.
Preparation of the Film

Quartz slides (25 mm 25 mm 1.5 mm) were cleaned with water, acetone, and chloroform in an ultrasonic bath for 30 min and dried in a hot air oven at $6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$for 3 h. The polymer was dissolved in chloroform, filtered with 0.45 nm syringe filter, and then spin-coated at 1000 rpm on to sonicated quartz slide and annealed around their $T _ { \mathrm { g } }$to yield dry amorphous film of good optical quality.
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Synthesis

A series of side-chain liquid crystalline polymethacrylates containing chalcone unit in the pendant were synthesized to investigate the photocrosslinking ability of chalcone moiety. The synthetic route of monomers and polymers are presented in

Scheme 1. The chemical structure of monomers and polymers was confirmed by FT-IR, <sup>1</sup>H and $^ { 1 3 } \mathrm { C }$NMR spectroscopy. The resonance signals for protons were assigned with alphabet as shown in the Figure (refer Supporting Information). The spectrum agrees well with targeted molecular structure of iia. The <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectrum of iia showed resonance signals at 6.88–8.14, 5.54 and 6.09, 2.21 ppm corresponding to aromatic, methacrylate vinyl, and methyl protons respectively. In addition, chalcone protons (<sub>A</sub>CH CH<sub>A</sub>) resonated at 7.26–7.39 ppm as doublet. After polymerization, the resonance signal at 2.21 ppm corresponding to a-methyl protons of monomer shifted up field by 0.5 ppm and merged with resonance signal of main-chain methylene protons in the polymers appeared at 1.59 ppm as broad signal. The representative <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectrum of Ia is shown in Figure 1.

Two series of polymers were prepared as a consequence of variations in the spacer lengths (x)

The thermal stability was estimated using TGA under nitrogen atmosphere at a heating rate of $1 0 ~ \mathrm { { ^ { \circ } C / m i n } }$. The thermograms show two stage decomposition transitions above $2 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$, indicating that all the polymers possess good thermal stability. The lower decomposition is probably resulted from cleavage of photocrosslinking moiety of chalcone unit while higher one is suggested to be the decomposition of methacrylate backbone. The thermal stability was evaluated by 5 and 50% weight loss at minimum temperature and data are illustrated in Table 2. The methyl substituted polymers (Ia–Ic) shows higher thermal stability than butyl substituted polymers (IIa–IIc). In general, the thermal stability was decreased with increasing spacer length from 6 to 10. It may be attributed to the presence of ether linkage in the spacer units were expected to introduce greater flexibility and consequently brought down thermal stability.<sup>6</sup> The decomposition was completed around $6 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$, and then no weight loss occurred. The char yield was measured at $8 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$. It shows that the char yield was increased with decreasing spacer length. In general, methyl substituted polymers (Ia–Ic) demonstrated higher char yield than butyl substituted polymers (IIa–IIc).

The liquid crystalline property of polymers was performed using DSC and POM studies. The DSC thermograms of second heating cycles of Ia–Ic and IIa–IIc are shown in Figures 2 and $^ { 3 , }$respectively, and extracted data summarized in Table 3. elements.text: remains on the substrate. The photochemical crosslinking reactions of Ia–IIc in solution and thin film were studied by UV irradiation at 365 nm. Figures 6 and 7 show absorption spectral pattern of Ia, IIa, and Ic, IIc in chloroform solution upon irradiation with UV light as a function of time, respectively. Before irradiation, chloroform solution Ia–Ic shows maxima around 398 nm and IIa–IIc shows around 403 nm corresponding to chalcone moiety. The absorption maxima of polymers in chloroform solution and thin film are summarized in Table 1. Upon irradiation with UV light, the intensity of absorption maximum were decreased ascribable to 2p 2p photocycloaddition of chalcone moiety (Scheme 2) and destroys conjugation in the entire p-electron system ensued in decrease of intensity as shown in Figures 6 and 7. Then, the reaction system reached photostationary state resulting change of color in solution from fluorescent to colorless as shown in Figure 8. After attaining photostationary state, in situ turbidity appeared in solution and when it was set aside, fine particles settle down in the cuvette as an indication of crosslinking that leads to insolubility in chloroform.

In the chalcone containing polymers prepared so for, the cis trans-isomerization reaction always compete with dimerization reaction of double bond upon irradiation under UV light.<sup>11,14,15,23</sup> On the other hand, in the present study, absorption spectral pattern clearly indicates without a isobestic point which responsible for cis trans-isomerization of chalcone double bond competing with dimerization reaction. It is attributed that the ionic interaction between two polymeric chains as shown in the Scheme 3 prevents isomerization of chalcone double bond upon irradiation with UV light. The concentration of chromophore also affects photocrosslinking reactions. When the concentration increases the time taken for decolorization increases due to ionic interactions as shown in Scheme 3. At the higher concentrations, interactions cited in Scheme 3 inhibit rate photocrosslinking reaction in chalcone double bond. At low chromophore contents, completion of decolorization taken place within 20 min.

At the same time, methyl group present in the third position may perturb close movement of chalcone unit for crosslinking reaction. The absorption spectral pattern of Ia–Ic and IIa–IIc obtained in chloroform and their relative rate of photocrosslinking are shown in Figure 9(a,b), respectively, where relative reactivity $A _ { \mathrm { o } } { - } A _ { \mathrm { t } } / A _ { \mathrm { o } }$is plotted against time of irradiation, in which $^ { 6 6 } { \cal A } _ { 0 } ^ { ~ 3 9 }$the absorption before irradiation and $^ { * } { \bf A } _ { \mathrm { t } } ^ { \ \mathrm { p } }$after irradiation at time $\mathbf { \omega } ^ { \mathfrak { s e } } { } _ { \mathbf { t } } \mathfrak { s }$. It suggests the spacer length x and y plays a significant role in photocrosslinking reaction of chalcone moiety. When x increases from 6 to 10, the rate of crosslinking also increased and indicated in Figure 9(a). In addition to this, the butyl substituted polymers exhibited faster crosslinking rate than methyl substituted polymers and depicted in Figure 9(b). The spacer was incorporated between mesogen and backbone as well as terminal position of mesogen to increase mobility of chromophore subsequently enhances crosslinking efficiency. Further, participation of chalcone double bond in photocrosslinking reaction was proved by infrared spectroscopy. The before and after irradiated FT-

The absorption maximum and shape of the spectra for solution and film were identical for all the polymers (Table 1), ascribed to mesogenic groups did not aggregate in coated film. The representative absorption spectral pattern of polymer Ib and IIb in thin film on quartz substrates are shown in Figure 11. Upon irradiation with UV light, decrease in absorption at 397 nm and 405 nm representing to 2p 2p photocycloaddition of chalcone moiety in thin film of Ib and IIb, respectively. In addition, the photocrosslinked polymer did not show liquid crystalline property attributed to restricted molecular mobility and attained rigidity by the polymer backbone.

elements.text: Fluorescence Property

The fluorescence emission spectra of polymers were measured in chloroform solution. They exhibited strong fluorescent emission in the range of 518–520 nm when excited with their absorption maximum due to ionic interactions as represented in Scheme 3. Upon irradiation with UV light, the absorption maximum was shifted to shorter wavelength in the range of 449–454 nm indicates the photocrosslinking reaction of chalcone moiety. The representative fluorescence spectral pattern of Ib upon irradiation with UV light is shown in Figure 12.

After crosslinking, the fluorescence maximum appeared at 519 nm corresponding to the indole moiety. Moreover, it was noted that all the polymers showed almost similar emission maxima in the emission spectra attributed to the emission is insensitive to irrespective of spacer length between the mesogen as well as in the terminal position.
CONCLUSIONS

The polymers were prepared by free-radical solution addition polymerization and characterized spectroscopically. The POM observations show that all the polymers exhibited grainy phase except Ic. The polymer Ic exhibited nematic phase at $1 8 7 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$The photocrosslinking reaction was monitored by UV-Vis spectrophotometer and fluorescence spectrofluorimeter. It displays the chalcone unit in the pendant is not showing cis trans-isomerization reaction along with $( 2 \pi + 2 \pi )$photodimerization upon irradiation with UV light like other chalcones reported so far. The photocrosslinking reaction of chalcone group was visibly monitored by change of fluorescent color to colorless. The spacer lengths play a key role in the photocrosslinking reaction. The fluorescence maximum was blue shifted by 70 nm in chloroform solution upon irradiation with UV light confirms the $2 \pi + 2 \pi$photodimerization of chalcone unit.
